case_scope: United States federal and state political-power channels relevant to wealth-order reform

democratic_nondomination_gate.note: Formal voting equality cannot certify wealth-order reform when independent expenditures, nontransparent funding, lobbying access, and local veto surfaces can pre-shape the feasible policy set.

large_donor_dependence.note: FEC scale data and comparative political-finance databases require donor-concentration, industry, candidate, ballot-measure, and state-level linking before a donor-dependence comfort score.

independent_expenditure_exposure.note: Independent-expenditure legality and 2023-2024 spending scale keep the U.S. case blocked until independent-spending surges are connected to wealth-order policy domains.

dark_money_or_nontransparent_spending.note: Brennan Center dark-money estimates remain a serious opacity trigger, but they are nonprofit research rather than official spending authority; use them to force source-chain disclosure evidence.

political_finance_enforcement_capacity.note: Enforcement capacity must be tested across federal, state, lobbying, ballot-measure, and transfer-chain data; federal filings alone do not cover the whole democratic-power rail.

lobbying_register_quality.note: Needs domain-specific read for tax, housing, finance, procurement, and platform policy influence.

local_land_use_veto.note: Homeowner/local-process veto converts existing housing wealth into entry closure when future residents, renters, and lower-wealth entrants cannot participate at equal practical weight.

reform_countermobilization_risk.note: Reforms threatening high-value rents require survival monitoring against spending, lobbying, litigation, and narrative reversal.

proof_debt: independent expenditure and dark-money source chains
industry lobbying tied to wealth-order bills
local land-use veto maps with renter/future-resident exclusion

gate_12_democratic_non_domination.why: Gate 12 remains blocked until campaign finance, dark-money, lobbying, state-level, local land-use, and post-enactment survival evidence show reform can survive concentrated wealth power.
